historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: equity 5yr CAGR 4.4% haircut to ~2% because the 2026 VAT reclassification permanently lowers the revenue level, communications-services revenue (68% of total) is now declining (-1.0% FY2025, -5.7% H1 2026) and the computing/AI growth (~20% of principal revenue) only offsets it over time
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.4% vs owner-FCF 5yr CAGR -8.5% (FY2020 117,952 -> FY2025 75,768): the FCF series is dominated by working-capital swings (FY2020 and FY2024 payables builds, FY2025 reversal) and the decline is not an earnings trend -- EPS compounded +3.6%/yr over the same window. Revenue 5yr CAGR 6.5% also exceeds the equity CAGR by >30% because 2021-2023 growth came from low-margin 'other businesses' (device sales) and DICT, not from the core. Flagged.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - SBC, with interest income left in place because it is received in investing activities and is already outside OCF. Lease payments are not deducted from the historical series (only disclosed FY2024-25) but are charged in every forward year. FY2018 736,819 / FY2020 768,070 / FY2022 937,259 / FY2025 1,050,187 revenue; FY2020 5.27 / FY2022 5.88 / FY2025 6.30 diluted EPS; equity FY2020 1,148,916 / FY2022 1,297,348 / FY2025 1,428,475.

scenario_narratives.base: The core communications business (68% of revenue) keeps shrinking 1-2%/yr as mobile ARPU erodes (RMB46.8, -3.5% FY2025; MOU -8.1%) and MIIT keeps tariffs capped, while computing (RMB89.8bn, AIDC +35%) and AI services (~RMB91bn) grow double digits and lift group revenue back to ~2% by FY2028. The January-2026 VAT reclassification (6% -> 9% on data/SMS/broadband) permanently resets the revenue and EBITDA level in year 1 and is never recovered. Capex follows guidance down to ~RMB137bn and stays ~13% of revenue as communications capex falls and computing/AI capex rises; the 75% payout (RMB103bn FY2025) is roughly all of owner FCF, so the RMB630bn+ broad cash pile is neither drawn nor grown. Associates are valued at market, not book, which strips ~RMB82bn of SPD Bank carrying value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Computing/AI scales faster than the base: AIDC and token-as-a-service demand make China Mobile the state-preferred AI-infrastructure utility, computing+AI pass 30% of principal revenue by FY2030, G&E revenue (RMB240bn, +6%) compounds, and the HKBN/international businesses add +30%/yr off a small base. Group growth reaches 4% in FY2028-30 with EBITDA margin recovering to 31% as 5G depreciation rolls off faster than the mix dilutes it; capex intensity falls to 12.5% as the communications network reaches steady state. Terminal cap 16x still sits well below global telecom-plus-cloud peers; no US-sanctions relief is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bear: ARPU decline accelerates (communications revenue -5.7% in H1 2026 is the run-rate, not a VAT artefact), a second fiscal squeeze follows the VAT change (the state uses the operators as a tax base), and the AI/computing pivot turns into a capex arms race against Alibaba/Tencent/Huawei Cloud with thin returns -- capex stays at 14% of revenue while EBITDA margin compresses to 27%. Leadership churn (Chairman, CEO and an ED gone within six months) slows execution. Terminal growth 1%, cap 12x -- closer to where the stock has actually traded. Even here the balance sheet is RMB568bn net cash, so the downside is an income-stock de-rating, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: China Mobile is valued as a mature, state-controlled telecom utility with a large non-operating balance sheet: roughly RMB568bn of broad net cash and RMB170bn of associates and equity investments against a market capitalisation of ~RMB1.49trn, so about half the market value is cash and investments and the core business trades at ~7x owner FCF, ~2.6x lease-consistent EV/EBITDA and a 6.6% dividend yield. The DCF credits the cash pile in full (the company's own broad liquidity definition, as for 9999.HK) and values listed associates at market rather than book. The resulting intrinsic value above the price is mostly the market's refusal to credit cash held inside a SASAC-controlled SOE at par plus the sanctions-driven investability discount; the required-return table shows what return the current price implies instead. Risk is charged once, in the scenario weights (25/50/25) and flows, not in a stacked WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Trapped-cash discount: the RMB633bn broad cash (of which RMB394bn is Level-3 wealth-management products) is credited at par; a holder cannot force its distribution and the state could direct it into AIDC capex or policy investments -- every 20% haircut on net cash is ~RMB5.2/share (~HK$6)
Further fiscal or tariff resets by decree (the 2026 VAT reclassification cost ~2pp of EBITDA margin in one stroke); a second such change is the bear case
Structural ARPU decline in communications (68% of revenue) outrunning computing/AI growth for longer than the base assumes
AI/computing capex arms race: FY2026 computing-network capex +62% -- if returns on AIDC lag, capex intensity does not fall to 13% and owner FCF stays near the FY2025 trough
Investability: NS-CMIC / 1260H listing bars US persons and most global mandates; the valuation gap may persist indefinitely, so the 15% hurdle entry price is the actionable number, not the IV
Associate values: SPD Bank carried RMB82bn above market; a formal impairment would hit reported profit (not cash) and could affect the 75%-of-profit dividend base
Receivables: G&E accounts receivable +RMB46bn since FY2024 on flat revenue; charged at ~0.7pp of margin, but a government-payment freeze would be larger

data_sources.financials: 0941.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, RMB millions) FY2018-FY2025 + H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026; FY2025 Annual Report (balance sheet p.82-83, cash flow p.85-87, notes 9, 10, 17(a), 21, 25, 38, 41, financial risk p.165); 2026 Interim Report (balance sheet p.14-15, cash flow p.18-19, notes 4 (VAT), 11(b), 12, 20(a)).
data_sources.qualitative: 0941.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-12): segment mix, ARPU trend, VAT reclassification, capex guidance RMB136.6bn, payout policy, NS-CMIC/1260H status, leadership changes.

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares for H1 2026 (21,780,966,909: 21,662.5m basic + 118.4m dilutive share-option equivalents; interim report note 11(b)). Issued shares at 30 June 2026 were 21,683,696,323. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (tiny, RMB200m FY2025) and option dilution is already in the diluted count.
inputs.cash_note: BROAD definition, as the company itself reports liquidity (FY2025 AR p.165: 'total cash and bank deposits, interest-bearing other financial assets at amortised cost and other debt investments, and WMPs and other investment products RMB652,048m'). 30 June 2026 balance sheet: cash & equivalents 102,438 + bank deposits 35,276 non-current + 85,419 current + other financial assets at amortised cost 6,893 + 9,014 + financial assets at FVTPL (wealth-management products / asset-management plans, Level 3) 259,830 + 133,883 = 632,753. FVOCI equity investments are NOT in cash; they sit in the equity bridge at fair value. The income these assets earn (RMB18.3bn FY2025: interest 5,292 + net gains on financial assets 13,011; average yield 2.70%) is excluded from EBITDA and received in INVESTING activities, so it is already outside reported OCF/FCF -- the matching-asset rule holds with no further deduction.
inputs.total_debt_note: Bank and other borrowings 9,374 (30 June 2026) + short-term deposits placed by CMCC Group with China Mobile Finance 55,762 (RMB40,005m at 31 Dec 2025, FY2025 AR note 41(a)/p.165, plus H1 2026 net receipts of 15,757). The CMCC deposits are interest-bearing parent funding and are treated as debt. Lease liabilities (46,186 current + 43,268 non-current = 89,454) are EXCLUDED under lease treatment (B).
inputs.interest_income_note: Set to 0 for the FCF-base deduction because China Mobile books 'Interest and other finance income received' (RMB8,199m FY2025) in INVESTING, not operating, cash flow; the P&L 'interest and other income' of RMB18,303m is reversed out of 'cash generated from operations'. Reported FCF therefore already excludes the yield on the cash pile. Deducting it again would double-strip. The pile itself is credited once, in net debt.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share options expenses' RMB200m (FY2024 489; FY2023 717). Share Option Scheme (note 38) is the only equity-settled plan; no net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0). SBC-near-zero market: house and street bases nearly coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2025 (RMB188m FY2024, 707m FY2022). Option exercises bring cash IN (RMB6,618m FY2025; 1,844 H1 2026); flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for, but the dilution it covers is already inside the diluted count.
inputs.fx_note: CNYHKD=X 1.1721 (Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-08). Direction: model (CNY) -> quote (HKD): HKD value = CNY value x 1.1721. All flows, cash and per-share values are computed in RMB (the statements' currency; the company reports 'Expressed in RMB') and converted to HKD once at the end. Parity check against the Shanghai A-share (600941.SS, RMB97.98 on 2026-10-09): the H-share price at inputs.price_as_of divided by 1.1721 lands at ~RMB68, an A/H premium of ~43% -- normal for Chinese SOE dual listings and NOT an fx error; the check is that the HKD price converted at 1/fx lands in RMB at the customary discount to the A share, which it does. Dividends are now declared in RMB (interim 2026 RMB2.51 = HK$2.9003 at the PBOC reference rate, a 1.1555 ratio in Aug-2026), so the valuation's RMB basis matches the cash a holder actually receives.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z (HKEX regular close, Friday 9 Oct 2026; market closed at valuation time -- not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% + ~6.2% premium = 8.0%. The premium is above a pure beta x ERP for a defensive utility (~5.5-6% would result) because (i) SOE governance: 68.7% CMCC/SASAC control, capital allocation directed partly by national policy (Eastern Data Western Computing, AIDC build-out), (ii) the investability discount: NS-CMIC / 1260H listing excludes US capital and most global mandates, so the marginal holder's required return is structurally higher. Risk is charged ONCE: the same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios; operating and regulatory outcomes (VAT, ARPU, AI pivot) live in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario WACC differences. Net cash company, so WACC = cost of equity.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full IFRS-16 lease payment (principal + interest, 'Repayment of principal and interest of lease liabilities' in financing: RMB33,798m FY2025, 3.2% of revenue; dominated by the China Tower Commercial Pricing Agreement running to 31 Dec 2027) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (RMB89,454m) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 D&A 189,999 less ROU depreciation 33,010 (AR note 17(a)) = 156,989, 14.95% of revenue, which is the da_pct_path anchor. Capex paths cover PP&E/intangibles only (lease renewals are inside the lease charge).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of EBITDA); NCI book value RMB4,410m (30 June 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI profit share is RMB169m/yr (0.1% of profit) -- 'No subsidiaries with NCI are material' (AR note 20).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (margins and capex intensity are still moving: VAT reclassification in year 1, communications-network capex falling while computing/AI capex rises, mix shifting toward lower-margin computing and device revenue). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating company, non-US, with material leases, a minority interest, large non-operating assets (RMB633bn broad cash, RMB218bn associates, RMB50bn FVOCI investments) and an SBC-near-zero market -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (a) currency, (b) leases, (c) NCI, (d) matching-asset rule, (e) SBC-zero, (f) charge risk once. Not a bank/REIT/LIC: China Mobile Finance is a captive treasury subsidiary, not a deposit-taking business line. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue 1,050,187; EBITDA 338,931 = profit from operations 148,932 + D&A 189,999, which EXCLUDES other gains, interest/other income and equity-accounted income, so the component build is clean of the stripped streams). RECEIVABLES: accounts receivable rose 75.7bn -> 99.8bn (FY2025) -> 122.2bn (H1 2026) on near-zero growth as the G&E mix grows; wc_capture on revenue change cannot see this, so the base EBITDA margin path is set ~0.7pp below the expected accounting margin to charge a recurring ~RMB7-8bn/yr receivables build (same device as 0788.HK). FY2025 reported FCF (75,968) is depressed by a RMB61bn working-capital outflow (payables/bills-payable reversal of FY2024's +59bn build); FY2024 (159,762) was flattered by the same swing. The normalised FY2025 pre-WC owner FCF is EBITDA 338.9 - lease 33.8 - cash tax 44.5 - capex 157.0 = ~RMB104bn, which is what the year-1 component build (~RMB108bn) should be compared against, and it is consistent with the FY2025 dividend of RMB103.4bn being paid while the cash pile held steady. VAT: from 1 Jan 2026 mobile data/SMS/broadband access moved from 6% to 9% VAT; VAT is excluded from revenue so the reclassification cuts reported revenue and EBITDA roughly one-for-one (H1 2026 revenue -1.1%, EBITDA -6.6%, profit -6.3%). It is permanent, so it is in the year-1 level and never 'recovers'. CAPEX: FY2026 guided RMB136.6bn company-basis (-9.5%); the cash-flow line runs ~RMB6bn higher (156,951 vs 150.9bn FY2025) because it includes intangibles/other non-current assets, so year-1 capex_pct 13.7% = ~RMB142.5bn on ~RMB1,040bn revenue. TAX: statutory 25%; FY2025 cash tax 44,479 on operating EBIT of ~147bn (after lease and ex-ROU D&A) less ~4.6bn attributable to the stripped financial income = ~27%; the deferred-tax-asset build (DTA 52bn -> 56bn) keeps cash tax above the P&L rate, so 26% is used, 27% in bear. SBC-ZERO: SBC 0.02% of revenue -- house and street values nearly coincide; the band is effectively a point and band_position should be read as n/a. Capex paths are PP&E/intangibles only; lease additions are inside the lease charge.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -1.0%: H1 2026 printed -1.1% with the VAT reclassification removing ~3pp of data/broadband revenue, partly offset by +11% other-business (device) revenue and computing/AI growth. FY2027 +1.5% as the VAT base effect laps; FY2028-31 +2.0% as computing/AI (~20% of principal revenue, growing double digits) outgrows a communications base shrinking ~1-2%/yr; fading to 1.5%. Ten-year revenue CAGR ~1.4%, below the 2% selected historical rate because the first year is negative.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 accounting EBITDA margin 32.3% (H2 alone 30.2%). FY2026 expected ~30.5% after the VAT step-down (H1 2026: 32.3% vs 34.2%). The path is set ~0.7pp below that to charge the recurring G&E receivables build (see inputs.notes), then drifts down 0.1pp/yr as computing/devices (lower margin) take mix share from communications.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guidance RMB136.6bn (-9.5%) company-basis = ~RMB142.5bn cash-flow basis = 13.7% of revenue; management is reallocating from communications network (falling) to computing (+62%) and AI (+20%) capex, so total intensity drifts to ~13.2% rather than collapsing. D&A ex-ROU (15.0%) converges toward capex over the decade as the 5G build (2019-23) rolls off.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8%/2% is 17x FCF; cap set at 15x for a mature, regulated, ex-growth utility -- the cap binds. The stock itself trades at ~7x core owner FCF (EV ex broad cash and associates ~RMB790bn vs ~RMB105bn), so even 15x embeds a re-rating; see valuation_philosophy.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: a single-regulator dependency (MIIT tariffs, MoF/STA tax policy -- the 2026 VAT change is a live example of the state resetting the operators' economics by decree) and a thesis that leans on an unproven pivot into AI/computing against better-resourced competitors. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right (computing scale, margin recovery, capex discipline, no further fiscal/sanctions tightening) and the NS-CMIC/1260H investability overhang caps any re-rating regardless of operating delivery.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
